claims.text: The initial alloy is equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi with a single-phase FCC structure.
The initial alloy has a grain size of approximately 20 µm.
Annealing at 500 °C for 100 h promotes chemical short-range order at grain boundaries.
Annealing at 1000 °C for 1 h retains a random solid solution.
The proposed grain-boundary CSRO consists of 2–5 nm clusters with element-specific enrichment and depletion.
Low-temperature annealing causes grain-boundary CSRO while deleterious intermetallic precipitation remains suppressed.
Grain-boundary CSRO reduces grain-boundary cohesive strength.
Impaired dislocation emission and reduced cohesion cause preferential intergranular cleavage rather than ductile transgranular failure.
The 500 °C-annealed alloy will show an approximately 20–30% decrease in K_IC relative to the initial baseline.
More than 50% of the fracture surface in the 500 °C-annealed alloy will be intergranular.
The as-processed baseline alloy has K_IC of approximately 200 MPa√m.
The baseline alloy fails predominantly by ductile transgranular dimpled fracture.
The proposed mechanism applies from 20 to 200 °C and at strain rates from 1×10^-5 to 1×10^-2 s^-1.
The proposed mechanism is limited to a single-phase FCC microstructure without external embrittling species.
The magnitude of toughness loss depends on CSRO volume fraction and cluster chemistry.
Failure to observe either a statistically significant toughness reduction or increased intergranular fracture after confirming CSRO would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome and falsification rule are expressed in K_IC, whereas the experiment specifies measurement of J_IC. These are distinct fracture-toughness metrics, and no conversion or common comparison criterion is provided.
